case.case_title: Rodrigo v Imalka Sub-Inspector of Police, Kirulapone and Others

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was unlawfully detained overnight without being brought before a judge as required by Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was detained overnight at the Fraud Bureau without prompt production before a Magistrate, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents argued the petitioner was detained to record a detailed statement and was produced before the Magistrate the next day.
key_facts: Petitioner was detained overnight at the Fraud Bureau after arrest.
No statement of the petitioner was recorded in the official Information Book.
Petitioner was produced before the Magistrate the next day on a Sunday and public holiday.
The detention was used to remand the petitioner without inquiry.
Magistrate discharged petitioner after verifying the licence’s authenticity.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any detained person be promptly brought before a judge and not held without legal order. Detention overnight without proper judicial oversight violates this right.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found the overnight detention was unjustified and that the recording of statements was fabricated. The petitioner was remanded without inquiry, violating Article 13(2).
principles_established: Detention must be followed by prompt production before a judicial authority.
Fabrication of statements to justify detention violates constitutional protections.
Remanding a detainee without inquiry breaches Article 13(2).
precedents_cited: Sarjun v Kamaldeen PC 39573 Police Station Habarana SCFR 559-03

outcome.holding: The Court declared that the petitioner’s fundamental right under Article 13(2) was infringed by unlawful detention without prompt judicial oversight.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation awarded as part of the overall remedy for fundamental rights violations.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) is central because the petitioner was detained overnight without being promptly brought before a judge, directly violating the constitutional safeguard against unlawful detention.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: Petitioner was detained overnight at the Fraud Bureau with no recorded statement and was produced before the Magistrate only the next day, resulting in remand without inquiry.
